The outlier is **Mq2**. Every other current-mirror PMOS (Mq0, Mq1, Mb2) is W=25.92 µm, L=0.15 µm, m=1, but Mq2 has m=3. That triples the pull-up current in stage 2 relative to the reference, so the stages are no longer matched. The stage-2 rise and fall delays differ, which distorts the ring's timing and compresses the range of frequencies the control voltage can reach. The measured fmax/fmin of about 2 (f_hi = 1.786 GHz vs. f_mid = 0.868 GHz) fits that compression. The main-path devices and the starving NMOS (Mc0–2) are consistent with each other, so the fault is isolated to the stage-2 pull-up multiplier.
